assumptions: frame members weighed as thin rods: density x area x length at the member centre
suspension arm bushings 3 kN/mm across the pivot axis (assumed: within passenger-car arm bushings, 1.7 to 5.0 kN/mm, no UTV value; the design has no bushing_radial_stiffness)
suspension arm bushings 0.5 kN/mm along the pivot axis (assumed: a little above passenger-car arm bushings, 0.23 to 0.46 kN/mm, no UTV value; the design has no bushing_axial_stiffness)
tie rod 10 kN/mm along its length, rack held (assumed, no source; the design has no tie_rod_stiffness)
K&C tables from the design's suspension hardpoints_mm, with their compliance from the bushings and the tie rod; longitudinal forces taken at the contact point

tyre forces: Magic Formula 6.1 with the coefficients of the 205/60R15 91 V, 2.2 bar (passenger car) tyre (H. B. Pacejka, Tire and Vehicle Dynamics, 3rd edition (2012), Appendix 3: the reference tyre's MF-Tyre parameters; not checked against the book). Not a measured UTV tyre: only the shapes of the passenger car tyre's curves are used, scaled to this vehicle: nominal load 1765 N (the mean static wheel load), R0 = the wheel radius, and at each wheel's static load the peak friction = mu and the slopes at zero slip = the stiffnesses K2 took (design or defaults above); held at the coefficients' nominal inflation pressure (no pressure terms, so nothing is extrapolated to a low-pressure tyre)

centres of pressure at the centroids of the part boxes and wheels projected on the side and front planes (along x always; the areas and the side centre's height only where the design does not give them) (assumed)
tip angles without the body's contact: right 42.106 deg, left 42.409 deg; the run tips to the right

body-to-ground contact: 26 points on the roll bar members (every 200 mm), 43 corners of the body's hull (frame nodes and sprung part boxes) and 48 on rings on the wheels' outer faces (0.8 x the radius, following the wheel's travel, the force into the body); each a penalty spring 1000 N/mm and damper 10000 N s/m along the road normal, Coulomb friction mu 2 regularised below 0.05 m/s (HIRAKU's choices, no source); the road is flat under each point; the peak forces and accelerations depend on the stiffness (max_contact_depth: the deepest sink; the _k2x results: the same run at twice the stiffness)
table surface friction 2 for the tyres and the body's contact points, so it tips, not slides
the table turned as the tilt tool turns it to the tip (42.11 deg), then at 4 deg/s to 43.11 deg and held; the brakes held

from the tip on the ground is the table and the level floor it is hinged on at its low edge (y = -1210 mm in the table frame, 500 mm outside the wheels: the table the tilt tool draws; HIRAKU's choice); the tip (the body's up axis past 60 deg), rest_tilt and rest_roll_world are to the floor (the world's up), max_roll, roll_turned, rest_roll and the record's roll to the table
stiffness_study = True from the analyze call's params (the load case gives True)
contact_stiffness = 1000 N/mm (assumed; neither the load case nor the design gives contact_stiffness)
